name: Platform economics

subjectOf.text: The platform's feedback loop is closed in the sense that there are no rent seeking owners: the system is entirely supported by its users and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.abstract: Therefore the feedback loop of the platform is closed, in the sense that there are no rent-seeking6 owners: The system is entirely supported by users, and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822
scope_conditions: all fees are disbursed to expert users
no outside owner holds a claim on fees

subjectOf.text: A healthy expertise tag requires that fees from new commenters buying in remain smaller in the long term than fees from outside business; otherwise the expertise tag is simply a pyramid scheme.
subjectOf.abstract: New commenter fees are expected to be smaller than outside business fees in the long term for healthy expertise tags; otherwise the expertise tag is simply a pyramid scheme.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822
scope_conditions: long term steady state of a mature expertise tag

subjectOf.text: Because decentralized platforms can remove the consumer fees that are integral to their centralized competitors, they also remove downward pressure on platform worker compensation, since costs are less likely to increase and be passed on to workers and consumers.
subjectOf.abstract: Removing such centralized fees also allows for the removal of downward pressure on the platforms' worker compensation as costs are less likely to increase and be passed on to workers and consumers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Systems Can Upgrade AI (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808867
scope_conditions: decentralized platforms with lower cost structures than centralized competitors

subjectOf.text: Computative Economics is not a generalization of digital platform economics, because platform economics extends Neoclassical Economics while remaining within its primitives, whereas the computative primitives differ and the equilibrium concept is recursive rather than competitive.
subjectOf.abstract: Computative Economics is not a generalization of platform economics. Its primitives differ. A computative agent is not a platform user in the platform-economic sense, and the equilibrium concept is recursive rather than competitive.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458
